docs.title: 🕹️ Redaplica Demo
docs.text:
Version: v0.1.0 · Built with [VIMz v2.1.0 Protocol] · StarkNet + Groth16 ZK

Redaplica is a zero-knowledge image reconstruction game built for pixel-art challenges, where players compete to “decrypt” redacted images without ever revealing their guesses.

This demo includes two core panels: the Creator Panel and the Player Panel. The game is structured into four main phases: Challenge Setup, Player Guessing, Reveal, and Scoring + Reward.

docs.title: 📁 Creator Panel
docs.text:
🛠️ NFT Challenge Creation Terminal

The Creator Panel allows users to upload pixel art, redact certain blocks, and publish a cryptographic commitment of the original image on StarkNet.

The main components of this panel are as follows:

  • Image Upload: Source image is processed into a 30×30 pixel matrix.
  • Redaction Matrix UI: Creator selects 10×10 pixel blocks to redact using an interactive block selector.
  • Hash-based Commitment Cacluation: Once redactions are finalized, a hash of the full original image is committed on-chain via a StarkNet smart contract.
  • Redacted Preview Generation: The system automatically generates a redacted version of the image by zeroing selected blocks.

docs.title: 🎮 Player Panel
docs.text:
✏️ NFT Reconstruction Interface

The Player Panel allows users to interactively reconstruct the redacted blocks by painting their guesses, and later submit a zero-knowledge proof of their accuracy.

The main components of this panel are as follows:

  • Pixel-Brush Tool: Players choose RGB colors to repaint redacted pixel.
  • Interactive Canvas: The player draws their guess directly onto the obfuscated image.
  • Commit to Answer: Upon completion, the player hashes their guessed image and commits it on-chain, without revealing it.

  • Proof Submission (Post-Reveal): After the challenger reveals the original, players locally compute their pixel-wise Hamming distance and generate a Groth16 proof showing:

  • Their guess matches their earlier commitment,

  • The score is correctly computed vs the revealed answer,
  • No information about their actual guess is leaked.

docs.title: 1.1. Creator uploads image
docs.text: • Using the "INITIALIZE NFT MATRIX"

docs.title: 1.3. Commits to original image hash on-chain
docs.text:
• By simply pressing "SUBMIT TO BLOCKCHAIN" button
  • From now on, the redacted image is updated as the newest challenge in the blockchain.

docs.title: 🧩 2. Player Phase
docs.text:
• Redacted image is published
  • Players try to reconstruct the missing pixels
  • Each player hashes their guess and commits it on-chain

docs.title: 🔓 3. Reveal Phase
docs.text:
• Creator reveals the original image
  • Players compare against their guesses locally

docs.title: 🧠 4. Scoring & ZK Proof
docs.text:
• Players generate Groth16 proofs of their score
  • Contract verifies proofs and selects the highest scorer
  • Winner receives NFT minted from the revealed image

docs.title: 📌 Notes
docs.text:
• All redactions and guesses are kept private until after scoring.
  • Groth16 verifier is integrated via Garaga and deployed in Cairo.
  • All answers are bound via the hash-based commitments.

docs.title: 🔐 Technical Overview
docs.text: This document describes the cryptographic mechanisms, protocol messages, and smart contract logic that make Redaplica a sound, complete, and trustless zero-knowledge game — without relying on any centralized server.

docs.title: ✅ Security Goals
docs.text:
Redaplica is designed to ensure the following properties:

  • Soundness: A player cannot fake a higher score than they deserve. Furthermore, the challenge creator cannot cheat or reveal a final solution other than the original NFT.
  • Completeness: A player who correctly reconstructs the image can prove it and their proof is successfully verifiable by all parties.
  • Zero-Knowledge: No player reveals their guess during any phase of the competition.
  • Non-Interactivity: All game logic is driven by public commitments and a final reveal. Hence, there are no interactions required between any player and the challenger.
  • Serverless Verifiability: The entire process can be verified on-chain without any centralized trusted third party.

docs.title: 🧩 Entities & Roles
docs.text:
• Creator – Publishes a redacted image challenge and commits to the original.
  • Player – Submits a guess (privately) and later proves their score using ZK.
  • Smart Contract – Verifies commitment openings and submitted proofs. Keeps record of the scores and finally, distributes rewards.

docs.title: 🔐 Cryptographic Primitives
docs.text: Component Scheme/Algorithm Purpose Hash Function Poseidon / Keccak Efficient commitments in SNARKs & Cairo ZK Proof System Groth16 Efficient proofs of score correctness ZK Verifier Garaga in Cairo On-chain Groth16 verification Score Function Hamming Distance Compares RGB differences over redacted pixels

docs.title: 1. Challenge Creation
docs.text:
Step Actor Message/Event 1 Creator Uploads image locally in browser 2 Creator Selects redacted blocks (e.g., 10×10 chunks) 3 Creator Computes C_img = Poseidon(Poseidon(original_image_bytes)\|\| r), where r acts as a random blinding factor. 4 Creator Calls contract.commit(C_img, redaction_spec) 5 Contract Stores hash commitment + metadata 6 Creator Publishes redacted version (zeroed blocks) to IPFS or a file server

➡️ No image is ever uploaded to a server. Commitment is purely on-chain.

docs.title: 2. Player Guessing
docs.text:
Step Actor Message/Event 1 Player Views redacted image 2 Player Reconstructs redacted regions (via UI) 3 Player Computes C_guess = Poseidon(Poseidon(guessed_pixels)\|\| r), where r acts as a random blinding factor. ` 4 Player Calls contract.submitGuess(challenge_id, C_guess)

➡️ Guess remains private. Only the hash is stored on-chain.

docs.title: 3. Reveal Phase
docs.text:
Step Actor Message/Event 1 Creator Publishes full NFT version to IPFS or a file server 2 Creator Calls contract.reveal(challenge_id, NFT_data, r) 3 Contract Verifies NFT_data against the commitment C_image 4 Contract Stores the H_redact corresponding to challenge_id

➡️ This is the only time the original image is revealed.

docs.title: 4. Score Proof Submission
docs.text:
Step Actor Message/Event 1 Player Locally computes score = Hamming(guess, original) 2 Player Generates Groth16 proof π_score stating that: my_score is Hamming(guess,orig) and I know r such that C_guess = Poseidon (Poseidon (guessed_pixels) \|\| r) 3 Player Calls contract.submitProof(challenge_id, π_score, my_score) 4 Contract Verifies proof using Garaga verifier contract against player's previously submitted commitment C_guess 5 Contract Stores the my_score corresponding to challenge_id and the player ID

➡️ Contract only accepts scores backed by a valid ZK proof.

docs.title: 5. Resolution & Reward
docs.text: Step Contract Action 1 Contract Tracks highest valid score 2 DAO/Contract After timeout, DAO calls contract.award(challenge_id, original_image_hash) function that mints NFT of original image to winner

docs.title: 🧠 Why It’s Trustless & Secure
docs.text: Property Mechanism No Server Trust All hashing, guessing, proof generation happens locally in browser No Guess Leakage Only commitments (C_guess) are published until proofs No Score Forgery ZK proof binds player to original guess and correct score No Creator Cheating Commitment to C_img ensures they can’t change original after seeing guesses Verifiability All checks (hash equality, proof verification) are enforced in the smart contract

docs.title: 📜 Smart Contract Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Store commitments (C_img, C_guess)
  • Validate revealed images against commitments
  • Verify Groth16 proofs using Garaga
  • Track highest valid score
  • Mint NFT of the final revealed image to the winning address
